revision_reason: Addressing plan reviewer feedback (needs_revision verdict): 5 issues identified covering missing gateway files, missing dag_visualizer tasks, missing sdlc_hitl.py _get_draft_path() task, pipeline starting phase ambiguity, and backward compatibility contradiction.
title: Add an interactive pre-refine step to the SDLC pipeline
summary: Architecture analysis for adding a conversational pre-refine phase where a human and Claude collaborate to produce a clear requirements document before the refine phase begins. The pre-refine step is fundamentally different from existing phases: it is human-driven and conversational rather than agent-driven with HITL gates. The recommended approach uses the existing egg-sdlc CLI to host the interactive session, adds a new PRE_REFINE pipeline phase, and stores the approved requirements document at .egg-state/drafts/{identifier}-requirements.md. The approved document replaces the original issue body/prompt as input to the refine phase. This revision addresses all 5 review feedback points: gateway phase infrastructure, dag_visualizer, sdlc_hitl.py _get_draft_path(), pipeline starting phase mechanism, and backward compatibility.

feedback_1_gateway_phase_infrastructure.issue: gateway/phase_filter.py has a third PipelinePhase enum (line 35), plus hardcoded PhasePermissions (lines 412-468) and PhaseFileRestriction (lines 490-530) dicts. gateway/phase_transition.py has its own VALID_TRANSITIONS dict (lines 41-46). None were mentioned in any task. The plan's backward compatibility claim that 'all existing phase switch/match/if-else chains handle the else/default case' is incorrect — these are explicit dict lookups that will raise KeyError or silently deny permissions.
feedback_1_gateway_phase_infrastructure.resolution: Added new tasks TASK-1-7 (gateway phase_filter.py) and TASK-1-8 (gateway phase_transition.py) to Phase 1. TASK-1-7 adds PRE_REFINE to the gateway's PipelinePhase enum, PhasePermissions dict (with minimal permissions matching pre_refine's read-only requirements-focused nature), and PhaseFileRestriction dict (allowing only .egg-state/drafts/*requirements* writes). TASK-1-8 adds PRE_REFINE -> [REFINE] to the gateway's VALID_TRANSITIONS dict. Updated the backward compatibility section to remove the incorrect claim about default/else handlers.
feedback_1_gateway_phase_infrastructure.investigation_findings: gateway/phase_filter.py:28-38 has PipelinePhase enum with comment 'Values must be kept in sync'. Lines 411-464 define PhasePermissions in _get_default_permissions() as an explicit dict with 4 entries (REFINE, PLAN, IMPLEMENT, PR). Lines 480-525 define PhaseFileRestriction in _get_default_phase_file_restrictions() as an explicit dict with 4 entries. gateway/phase_transition.py:41-46 defines VALID_TRANSITIONS as an explicit dict with 4 entries. All are explicit lookups that would KeyError on unknown phases.

feedback_2_dag_visualizer.issue: orchestrator/dag_visualizer.py has hardcoded PHASE_ORDER list (lines 49-54) and PHASE_NAMES map (lines 57-62). Without updating these, pipeline visualization will not show PRE_REFINE.
feedback_2_dag_visualizer.resolution: Added new task TASK-1-9 to Phase 1 to update dag_visualizer.py. PRE_REFINE is inserted at index 0 of PHASE_ORDER (before REFINE) and added to PHASE_NAMES with display name 'Pre-Refine'. This ensures DAG rendering, compact status, progress bars, and report generation all include the new phase.
feedback_2_dag_visualizer.investigation_findings: dag_visualizer.py:49-54 defines PHASE_ORDER = [REFINE, PLAN, IMPLEMENT, PR]. Lines 57-62 define PHASE_NAMES = {REFINE: 'Refine', PLAN: 'Plan', IMPLEMENT: 'Implement', PR: 'PR'}. These are used in DAG rendering (line 372), compact status (line 530), progress bar (line 562), and report generation (line 636).

feedback_3_sdlc_hitl_get_draft_path.issue: TASK-2-2 updates _get_draft_path() in orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py, but there is a parallel _get_draft_path() in sandbox/egg_lib/sdlc_hitl.py:27 (comment says 'Mirrors the logic in orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py'). The CLI won't resolve the requirements draft path for pre_refine.
feedback_3_sdlc_hitl_get_draft_path.resolution: Added new task TASK-3-5 to Phase 3 to update sdlc_hitl.py:_get_draft_path() to handle the pre_refine phase. The function at line 43 currently has special cases for 'refine' (returns analysis.md) and 'implement' (returns None), with a generic fallback. The fallback would produce '{prefix}-pre_refine.md' which is incorrect — it should produce '{prefix}-requirements.md'. An explicit branch for phase == 'pre_refine' is needed before the generic fallback.
feedback_3_sdlc_hitl_get_draft_path.investigation_findings: sdlc_hitl.py:27-48 defines _get_draft_path() with explicit branches for 'refine' -> analysis.md and 'implement' -> None, and a generic else branch that produces {prefix}-{phase}.md. The docstring at line 35 says 'Mirrors the logic in orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py:_get_draft_path'. Without explicit handling, 'pre_refine' would fall through to the generic else and produce '{prefix}-pre_refine.md' instead of '{prefix}-requirements.md'.

feedback_4_pipeline_starting_phase.issue: No task specifies how a pipeline with skip_pre_refine=false starts at PRE_REFINE instead of REFINE. Pipeline model defaults to current_phase=PipelinePhase.REFINE (models.py:247). If the pipeline starts at REFINE, the PRE_REFINE code path is never reached.
feedback_4_pipeline_starting_phase.resolution: The mechanism is: pipeline creation logic (not the model default) conditionally sets the starting phase. The Pipeline model default stays REFINE for backward compatibility. The change goes in _run_pipeline() at startup: before entering the phase loop, check PipelineConfig.skip_pre_refine — if false AND no existing requirements document, set current_phase to PRE_REFINE. This is specified in TASK-2-1 (updated description). The model default is NOT changed — this preserves backward compatibility for existing callers that create pipelines directly without going through _run_pipeline(). This approach is cleanest because: (1) it avoids changing the model default which would break all existing pipeline creation paths, (2) it keeps the phase-starting logic co-located with the phase-running logic in _run_pipeline(), and (3) it naturally handles the re-run case (if requirements already exist, skip pre-refine).
feedback_4_pipeline_starting_phase.investigation_findings: Pipeline model at models.py:247 has current_phase=PipelinePhase.REFINE as Field default. Pipeline creation in state_store.py:574-584 does NOT set current_phase explicitly. Routes create_pipeline in routes/pipelines.py:483-491 (local) and 529-536 (issue) call store.create_pipeline() which instantiates Pipeline with the default. The cleanest approach is to have _run_pipeline() check config and set current_phase to PRE_REFINE at startup, rather than changing the model default.

feedback_5_backward_compatibility.issue: Plan states skip_pre_refine defaults to false (pre-refine enabled) but also says existing callers get current behavior (start at REFINE). These are inconsistent — if default is false, existing callers would get pre-refine enabled.
feedback_5_backward_compatibility.resolution: Resolved the contradiction. The skip_pre_refine field on PipelineConfig defaults to true (opt-in model). This means: (1) existing pipeline creation paths that don't set skip_pre_refine get skip_pre_refine=true, preserving the current behavior of starting at REFINE; (2) callers that explicitly want pre-refine set skip_pre_refine=false; (3) the egg-sdlc CLI's interactive mode sets skip_pre_refine=false by default (the CLI is the primary entry point for human-interactive use); (4) headless/CI callers don't pass the flag and get the default (true = skip). This decouples the config default (backward-compatible) from the CLI default (user-friendly).
feedback_5_backward_compatibility.investigation_findings: The contradiction arose from conflating two defaults: the PipelineConfig field default (which must be backward-compatible) and the CLI's default behavior (which can be opinionated). Solution: PipelineConfig.skip_pre_refine defaults to true. The egg-sdlc CLI explicitly passes skip_pre_refine=false when running interactively. This gives backward compatibility for all programmatic callers while making pre-refine the default for interactive CLI users.

problem_statement.description: The SDLC pipeline currently starts at the refine phase, where an agent autonomously analyzes an issue and produces an analysis document. If the original issue/prompt is poorly defined, the refine agent may produce a low-quality analysis, leading to wasted cycles through multiple HITL revision loops or cascading misunderstandings through plan and implement. There is no structured mechanism for a human to collaboratively clarify requirements before autonomous work begins.
goals: Add a conversational pre-refine step where human and Claude collaborate to produce a clear requirements document
The step must be interactive and free-form (back-and-forth conversation, not structured HITL checkboxes)
Support both issue mode (GitHub issue) and local mode (no GitHub)
Produce a single requirements document with: problem statement, functional requirements, constraints, acceptance criteria, and any other context
Human must explicitly approve the requirements document before advancing to refine
The approved document replaces the original issue body/prompt as the direct input to the refine phase
In issue mode, update the GitHub issue description with the approved requirements document
No codebase interaction during pre-refine — purely requirements-focused

pipeline_phases.mechanism: PipelinePhase enum defines exactly 4 phases: REFINE, PLAN, IMPLEMENT, PR. Each pipeline tracks current_phase and per-phase execution state. Default current_phase is PipelinePhase.REFINE (line 247).
pipeline_phases.constraint: Adding a new phase requires updating the enum in THREE locations (orchestrator/models.py, shared/egg_contracts/models.py, gateway/phase_filter.py), plus phase transitions in TWO locations (orchestrator/routes/phases.py, gateway/phase_transition.py), plus explicit dict lookups in gateway/phase_filter.py (PhasePermissions, PhaseFileRestriction) and orchestrator/dag_visualizer.py (PHASE_ORDER, PHASE_NAMES).

phase_transitions.mechanism: Both files define phase transition dicts. Orchestrator: PHASE_TRANSITIONS maps REFINE -> [PLAN, IMPLEMENT], PLAN -> [IMPLEMENT], IMPLEMENT -> [PR], PR -> []. Gateway: VALID_TRANSITIONS maps REFINE -> [PLAN], PLAN -> [IMPLEMENT], IMPLEMENT -> [PR], PR -> []. Note: orchestrator allows REFINE -> IMPLEMENT (short-circuit) which gateway does not.
phase_transitions.constraint: Adding PRE_REFINE requires updating BOTH transition maps. PRE_REFINE -> [REFINE] in both.

gateway_phase_filter.mechanism: Contains a THIRD PipelinePhase enum (line 28-38, comment: 'Values must be kept in sync'), PhasePermissions dict (lines 411-464 in _get_default_permissions()), and PhaseFileRestriction dict (lines 480-525 in _get_default_phase_file_restrictions()). All are explicit dict lookups that will KeyError on unknown phases.
gateway_phase_filter.constraint: PRE_REFINE must be added to all three structures. PhasePermissions must define allowed/blocked operations. PhaseFileRestriction must define allowed file patterns (only .egg-state/drafts/*requirements*).

dag_visualizer.mechanism: PHASE_ORDER list (lines 49-54) and PHASE_NAMES dict (lines 57-62) are hardcoded with 4 phases. Used in DAG rendering (line 372), compact status (line 530), progress bar (line 562), and report generation (line 636).
dag_visualizer.constraint: PRE_REFINE must be added to PHASE_ORDER (at index 0, before REFINE) and PHASE_NAMES (display name: 'Pre-Refine').

pipeline_orchestration.mechanism: _run_pipeline() is the main background thread. It loops through phases, spawning agent containers, running review cycles, and pausing for HITL approval. Each phase runs one or more agent containers via _spawn_and_wait().
pipeline_orchestration.key_detail: All existing phases follow the pattern: spawn non-interactive agent container in --print mode -> wait for exit -> read artifacts -> optionally review -> HITL gate. Pre-refine breaks this pattern because it requires an interactive, conversational session rather than a headless agent run.

pipeline_creation.mechanism: Pipeline is instantiated in state_store.create_pipeline() without setting current_phase explicitly. It defaults to PipelinePhase.REFINE from the model Field default. Routes create_pipeline has two paths: local mode (lines 483-491) and issue mode (lines 529-536), both calling store.create_pipeline().
pipeline_creation.key_detail: The starting phase must be set by _run_pipeline() logic, not by changing the model default, to preserve backward compatibility for all creation paths.

hitl_handling.mechanism: handle_hitl_checkpoint() presents a 5-option menu when pipeline pauses: edit with $EDITOR, launch Claude, approve, provide feedback, cancel. This is the closest existing infrastructure to an interactive step but is post-phase (runs after agent completes), not in-place-of a phase.
hitl_handling.key_detail: Option 2 ('Launch Claude for AI-assisted editing') already spawns an interactive Claude Code session with context about the current draft. This pattern is adapted for pre-refine.

cli_draft_path.mechanism: _get_draft_path() mirrors orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py:_get_draft_path(). Has explicit branches for 'refine' -> analysis.md and 'implement' -> None, with generic else -> {prefix}-{phase}.md. The generic fallback would produce '{prefix}-pre_refine.md' which is WRONG — it must produce '{prefix}-requirements.md'.
cli_draft_path.key_detail: An explicit branch for pre_refine is required in this function. Cannot rely on the generic fallback.

cli_pipeline_watch.mechanism: watch_pipeline() connects to SSE stream and monitors events. When pipeline status is 'awaiting_human', it calls handle_hitl_checkpoint(). The watch loop handles reconnection and terminal states.
cli_pipeline_watch.key_detail: The watch loop is where the egg-sdlc CLI interacts with the human. Pre-refine must integrate here.

prompt_building.mechanism: _build_phase_prompt() constructs phase-specific prompts for agent containers. Refine prompt includes the issue body/prompt and asks for analysis. Plan prompt includes the prior analysis.
prompt_building.key_detail: The refine prompt currently receives the raw issue body/prompt. Pre-refine would replace this with the approved requirements document.

phase_permissions_json.mechanism: Each phase defines allowed/blocked operations and file patterns. Refine allows gh issue comment/edit, git push for state files, and egg-contract operations.
phase_permissions_json.key_detail: Pre-refine would need minimal permissions — no code changes, no PRs. Only needs to write the requirements document to .egg-state/drafts/.

local_mode_input.mechanism: run_local_mode() already has a basic interactive prompt: 'What would you like to build or change?' and 'Any specific files?'. This input becomes pipeline.prompt which is passed directly to the refine agent.
local_mode_input.key_detail: Pre-refine for local mode would replace this simple prompt with a richer conversational requirements gathering session.

draft_management.mechanism: _get_draft_path() returns phase-specific paths. Refine: {prefix}-analysis.md, Plan: {prefix}-plan.md. The prefix is pipeline_id (local) or issue_number (issue mode).
draft_management.key_detail: Pre-refine would add a new draft type: {prefix}-requirements.md.

approaches.name: New PRE_REFINE pipeline phase with interactive Claude session (recommended)
approaches.description: Add PRE_REFINE as a first-class pipeline phase. When the pipeline enters pre-refine, the orchestrator pauses (AWAITING_HUMAN) and the egg-sdlc CLI launches an interactive Claude Code session configured with a requirements-gathering system prompt. Claude asks probing questions, the human responds conversationally, and together they produce a requirements document. When the human approves, the CLI writes the document to .egg-state/drafts/{identifier}-requirements.md, resolves the HITL decision, and the pipeline advances to REFINE with the requirements document as input.
pros: Clean separation of concerns: pre-refine is its own phase with its own state tracking
Fits naturally into the existing phase lifecycle: status tracking, SSE events, visualization all work
The interactive Claude session is already a proven pattern (HITL option 2 uses the same mechanism)
Pipeline can be restarted/resumed from pre-refine if interrupted
Phase permissions can restrict pre-refine to only requirements document writes
Pipeline visualization correctly shows PRE_REFINE as a distinct step
DAG visualization and SSE stream events work without special casing
cons: New enum value touches many code paths: 3 PipelinePhase enums, 2 transition maps, gateway PhasePermissions/PhaseFileRestriction dicts, dag_visualizer PHASE_ORDER/PHASE_NAMES
Existing pipelines created before the change won't have PRE_REFINE state
The interactive session breaks the existing pattern of non-interactive agent containers
Requires careful handling of the phase in issue mode (no container to spawn for pre-refine)

approaches.name: Pre-pipeline CLI step (no new phase)
approaches.description: Instead of adding a new pipeline phase, run the requirements gathering session entirely within the egg-sdlc CLI before creating the pipeline. The CLI launches an interactive Claude session, produces a requirements document, and then creates the pipeline with the requirements as the prompt/issue body. No orchestrator changes needed.
pros: No changes to the orchestrator, phase enum, or pipeline state
Simpler implementation — entirely in the CLI layer
No new phase to handle in visualization, SSE events, etc.
cons: Requirements gathering is invisible to the pipeline — no state tracking, no restart capability
Cannot skip pre-refine for well-defined issues (always runs or needs an explicit flag to skip)
In issue mode, the requirements doc exists only as the modified issue body — no separate artifact
Cannot be monitored via SSE stream or visualized in the DAG
If the CLI crashes during requirements gathering, all work is lost (no checkpoint)
Not composable with headless/CI pipeline triggers — only works with interactive CLI

approaches.name: Reuse HITL gate at refine phase start
approaches.description: Instead of a new phase, add an optional HITL gate at the start of the refine phase. When the pipeline reaches REFINE, it immediately pauses (AWAITING_HUMAN) and presents the original issue/prompt for collaborative refinement. The human uses the existing HITL menu to produce a requirements document. On approval, the refine agent runs with the refined input.
pros: No new phase — reuses existing HITL infrastructure
Minimal orchestrator changes — just add a pre-agent HITL gate to refine
Backward compatible — gate can be optional (controlled by config)
Works with existing SSE events and visualization (shows as AWAITING_HUMAN in refine phase)
cons: Conflates two distinct concepts (requirements gathering vs. analysis review) in one phase
The HITL menu is designed for post-phase artifact review, not conversational requirements gathering
No separate requirements artifact — the refined input replaces the original prompt in-place
The refine phase HITL gate (post-agent) becomes confusable with the pre-agent gate
Pipeline status shows 'refine/awaiting_human' for both pre-refine requirements AND post-refine review, making it hard to tell them apart in monitoring

recommended_approach.name: New PRE_REFINE pipeline phase with interactive Claude session
justification: A new phase provides clean separation of concerns. Pre-refine is conceptually distinct from analysis (refine): it's human-driven requirements gathering, not agent-driven codebase analysis. Modeling it as its own phase makes this distinction explicit in the system's state machine.

The existing HITL infrastructure (decision queue, _launch_claude() in sdlc_hitl.py) already supports the interactive Claude session pattern needed for pre-refine. The main new work is: (1) the requirements-gathering system prompt, (2) writing the requirements document, and (3) plumbing the new phase through the orchestrator and gateway.

Approach B (pre-pipeline CLI step) loses state tracking and restart capability. If the user's terminal disconnects during a long requirements session, all work is lost. With a phase, the pipeline knows it's in pre-refine and can resume.

Approach C (HITL gate at refine start) conflates two different HITL pauses in the same phase. Pipeline monitoring cannot distinguish 'waiting for requirements' from 'waiting for analysis review'. A separate phase makes pipeline state unambiguous.

The issue explicitly states pre-refine should work in both local and issue modes. A first-class phase naturally supports both through the same orchestration loop, while Approach B would require separate handling for each mode.

The enum change (adding PRE_REFINE) requires updating 3 enum definitions, 2 transition maps, 2 gateway dicts, and 1 visualizer — more than originally estimated but still a well-understood pattern. The codebase already handled adding the PR phase and the short-circuit REFINE -> IMPLEMENT transition.

technical_decisions.decision: Model pre-refine as a first-class pipeline phase (PRE_REFINE)
technical_decisions.rationale: Clean state machine semantics. Pipeline status unambiguously shows whether the system is gathering requirements (pre_refine) vs. running analysis (refine). Enables state tracking, restart from pre-refine, SSE events, and visualization. The alternative (pre-pipeline CLI step) loses all observability.
alternatives_considered: Pre-pipeline CLI step — rejected: no state tracking, no restart, invisible to monitoring
HITL gate at refine start — rejected: conflates two HITL pauses in one phase, ambiguous pipeline status

technical_decisions.decision: Use interactive Claude Code session (not headless agent container) for requirements gathering
technical_decisions.rationale: The issue explicitly states pre-refine should be 'interactive and conversational (free-form back-and-forth, not structured HITL checkboxes)'. The existing _launch_claude() pattern in sdlc_hitl.py provides exactly this. A headless agent container cannot support real-time human conversation.
alternatives_considered: Multi-turn HITL decision loop — rejected: too rigid, not conversational
Headless agent with periodic HITL pauses — rejected: breaks conversational flow

technical_decisions.rationale: Follows the existing draft management pattern (analysis.md for refine, plan.md for plan). The identifier is the issue number (issue mode) or pipeline ID (local mode). The file is committed to the feature branch for auditability.
alternatives_considered: Store in issue body only — rejected: no artifact for local mode, no separate file for the refine agent to read
Store in contract JSON — rejected: requirements are prose, not structured data

technical_decisions.decision: PipelineConfig.skip_pre_refine defaults to true (opt-in model for backward compatibility)
technical_decisions.rationale: Resolves the backward compatibility contradiction identified in review feedback #5. The PipelineConfig field default must be true (skip) so that all existing callers that create pipelines without passing this flag get the current behavior (start at REFINE). The egg-sdlc CLI's interactive mode explicitly sets skip_pre_refine=false (pre-refine enabled). This decouples the config default (backward-compatible) from the CLI default (user-friendly). Headless/CI callers that don't pass the flag naturally skip pre-refine.
alternatives_considered: Default false (always enable pre-refine) — rejected: breaks backward compatibility for all existing pipeline creation paths
Change Pipeline model default to PRE_REFINE — rejected: would affect all pipeline instantiation including internal/test code

technical_decisions.decision: Pipeline starting phase is set by _run_pipeline() logic, not by changing the Pipeline model default
technical_decisions.rationale: Resolves review feedback #4. The Pipeline.current_phase default stays PipelinePhase.REFINE. In _run_pipeline(), at startup before the phase loop, the function checks PipelineConfig.skip_pre_refine: if false AND no existing requirements document, it sets pipeline.current_phase to PRE_REFINE. This approach: (1) preserves backward compatibility for all pipeline creation paths, (2) co-locates phase-starting logic with phase-running logic, (3) naturally handles re-runs (if requirements exist, stay at REFINE).
alternatives_considered: Change Pipeline model default to PRE_REFINE — rejected: would force all callers to handle the new phase
Set starting phase in pipeline creation routes — rejected: would require changes in multiple creation paths and miss internal/test creation
Conditional model default based on config — rejected: Pydantic model defaults shouldn't have complex logic

technical_decisions.decision: In issue mode, update the GitHub issue description with approved requirements
technical_decisions.rationale: The issue states: 'In issue mode, the issue description on GitHub is updated with the approved requirements document.' This ensures the issue body is the canonical source of requirements. The original issue body is preserved in a collapsed <details> section for context.
alternatives_considered: Post as a comment — rejected: refine agent reads the issue body, not comments
Only store in .egg-state file — rejected: issue description would be stale

technical_decisions.decision: No codebase interaction during pre-refine — Claude has no access to repository files
technical_decisions.rationale: The issue explicitly states: 'No codebase interaction — purely requirements-focused.' The Claude session should be configured without repository access to prevent scope creep into analysis. The refine agent handles codebase research.
alternatives_considered: Allow read-only codebase access — rejected: violates issue requirement, blurs line between pre-refine and refine

technical_decisions.decision: The pre-refine orchestrator phase immediately pauses (AWAITING_HUMAN) rather than spawning a container
technical_decisions.rationale: Pre-refine is human-driven. The orchestrator's role is to track state and wait, not to run an agent. The interactive Claude session is launched by the CLI (client-side), not the orchestrator (server-side). This matches the existing HITL pattern where the CLI handles human interaction.
alternatives_considered: Spawn a container that runs an interactive session — rejected: containers are non-interactive in the current architecture (--print mode)

risks.description: PRE_REFINE enum value requires updating all phase-handling code paths across 3 enum definitions, 2 transition maps, and multiple explicit dict lookups
risks.mitigation: Phase 1 comprehensively enumerates all locations: orchestrator/models.py, shared/egg_contracts/models.py, gateway/phase_filter.py (enum + PhasePermissions + PhaseFileRestriction), gateway/phase_transition.py, orchestrator/routes/phases.py, orchestrator/dag_visualizer.py, .egg/phase-permissions.json, shared/egg_contracts/phase_defaults.py. Each is a discrete, additive change.

risks.description: Interactive Claude session may not work in all deployment modes (e.g., headless CI)
risks.mitigation: skip_pre_refine defaults to true in PipelineConfig. Only the interactive CLI explicitly sets it to false. Headless/CI callers skip pre-refine by default.

risks.description: Requirements document quality depends on human engagement
risks.mitigation: Claude's system prompt should guide the conversation with probing questions. The refine agent still performs its own analysis, so pre-refine is additive quality improvement, not a replacement for analysis.

risks.description: Backward compatibility with existing pipelines that don't have PRE_REFINE state
risks.mitigation: Pipeline model default stays REFINE. skip_pre_refine defaults to true. Only interactive CLI callers opt in. Existing pipelines in any phase continue to work. Phase transition validation accepts REFINE as a starting phase.

risks.description: Claude session crash or disconnect during requirements gathering loses work
risks.mitigation: Claude writes to the requirements file incrementally during the conversation. Even if the session crashes, partial work is saved. The pipeline remains in PRE_REFINE/AWAITING_HUMAN state, so the human can resume by reattaching to the pipeline.

risks.description: _get_draft_path() in sdlc_hitl.py gets out of sync with orchestrator version
risks.mitigation: TASK-3-5 explicitly addresses this. The function already has a comment saying 'Mirrors the logic in orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py:_get_draft_path'. The pre_refine branch must produce {prefix}-requirements.md (NOT {prefix}-pre_refine.md which the generic fallback would produce).

constraints: Pre-refine must be purely conversational — no structured HITL checkboxes for requirements gathering
No codebase interaction during pre-refine — Claude should not access repository files
Must work in both issue mode and local mode
Must be skippable for well-defined issues and headless CI execution
In issue mode, GitHub issue description is updated with approved requirements
Human must explicitly approve before advancing to refine
Backward compatible: existing pipelines without pre-refine continue to function — PipelineConfig.skip_pre_refine defaults to true, Pipeline.current_phase default stays REFINE
The approved requirements document becomes the direct input to the refine phase, replacing the original issue body/prompt
PRE_REFINE must be added to all three PipelinePhase enum locations (orchestrator, contracts, gateway)
Gateway PhasePermissions and PhaseFileRestriction dicts must include PRE_REFINE (explicit dict lookups, no default/fallback)

open_questions.question: Should the requirements-gathering Claude session have read-only access to the repo structure (file listing) to help the human identify relevant areas?
open_questions.recommendation: No — the issue explicitly says 'no codebase interaction'. Keep pre-refine purely requirements-focused. The human can mention files/areas in conversation if needed.
open_questions.impact: Low — can be added later if needed

open_questions.question: Should the requirements document follow a strict template or be free-form?
open_questions.recommendation: Guide with a suggested structure (problem statement, functional requirements, constraints, acceptance criteria) but allow deviation. Claude's system prompt suggests the structure; the human can override.
open_questions.impact: Low — template can be refined based on usage

open_questions.question: How should the original issue body be preserved when updated with requirements in issue mode?
open_questions.recommendation: Include the original issue body in a collapsed <details> section at the bottom of the requirements document. This preserves context while making the requirements the primary content.
